## Description

Colonial peritrich ciliate with zooids of ~100 µm on branched stalks. Unlike *Zoothamnium*, the
spasmoneme of each branch is independent (it is interrupted at the bifurcations), so each zooid
contracts on its own.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 1 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [branched colony](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md#branched-colonies) of up to 12 zooids on spasmoneme
stalks without a shared spasmoneme. Each zooid is a bell (`profile = "bell"`) that closes its
peristome and rounds up in milliseconds when stimulated and reopens in seconds. It divides
longitudinally; one daughter leaves as a telotroch (short cylinder, aboral pole first). Stalk width,
bending and branch angle estimated.

## Not implemented yet

- The colony does not grow beyond 12 zooids (real colonies have hundreds).
- Stalks do not collide with cells ([bug](../../bugs/stalks-and-tails-do-not-collide.md)).

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares [spasmoneme stalks](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md) with *Vorticella* and *Zoothamnium*,
[bell contraction](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) with all peritrichs, and
[longitudinal division](../../mechanics/life-cycle-and-division.md). The independent spasmoneme per branch
distinguishes it from *Zoothamnium*.
